Yes, strawberries generally have more vitamin C than oranges, though the comparison depends on the measurement used. On a per-100g basis, strawberries contain 59 mg of vitamin C, which exceeds what 100g of oranges contain [d2]. Per cup, strawberries provide 85–89 mg of vitamin C, compared to approximately 70 mg in one medium orange [d3][d8]. By weight, strawberries are also said to contain more vitamin C than citrus fruits including oranges and grapefruit [d4][d7]. One source notes that a single serving of strawberries can account for more than 160% of the recommended daily intake of vitamin C [d5]. However, on a per-individual-berry basis, a single large strawberry contains only about 10.5 mg, meaning you would need at least seven strawberries to exceed the vitamin C in one orange [d1], and one source describes strawberries as "on par" with oranges at 120% of the RDI [d6]. Taken together, strawberries do have more vitamin C than oranges when compared by weight or standard serving size (per cup), but the advantage depends on how the comparison is framed.
